summary: The locked record covers 2 completed experiments in 0.3 minutes: 1 compute-bound task and 1 synthesis-only task. The compute-bound entry was recorded at 0.0 minutes, and the locked compute-task GPU-idle indicator is false.
bottlenecks_identified: The disk-mtime fallback recorded the compute-bound experiment at 0.0 minutes, so no data available this milestone explains which execution phase took the longest.
The GPU snapshot is not tied to task start, phase, and finish boundaries, so it cannot establish utilization efficiency throughout the compute task.
No data available this milestone establishes that 2 or more models were loaded in parallel or records runner selection, so a DualGPURunner dispatch failure cannot be assessed.
improvements_suggested: Batch 8-16 questions per forward pass on the single inference process and record the realized throughput change.
Capture monotonic queue, model-load, inference, verification, and artifact-write timestamps in each task receipt.
Join task identity and phase boundaries to GPU utilization samples.
Persist loaded-model count, sequential-versus-parallel mode, and runner identity; use the second GPU only when 2 or more models are actually loaded in parallel.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Add configurable 8-16 question batching to the inference path.
Replace timing-floor diagnosis with task-owned monotonic phase telemetry.
Record task-scoped GPU samples, model concurrency, and runner selection in one launch receipt.
meta_reflection: The snapshot shows active compute on one GPU and therefore does not support a compute-idle defect, but it cannot explain the task's phase costs. Batching is the clearest throughput change suggested by the evidence; milestone-wide savings remain unmeasured, so the estimate stays at 0%.
